mainTopic: The limits of the שהייה tradition for a טמא person in the מקדש, and whether the long-way and short-way rule is about route or time
overview: The גמרא has a tradition (גמירי) that a person who becomes טמא inside the מקדש is liable only if he stays there for a set time (שהייה), the time it takes to bow down. First come four questions that test how far this tradition reaches: lashes as well as a קרבן, someone hanging in the air of the עזרה, someone who made himself טמא on purpose, and a נזיר at a grave outside the מקדש. Each ends with תיקו. Then the גמרא returns to the משנה's rule that leaving by the long way is חייב and by the short way is פטור. רבא says the short way is פטור even if he walks heel-to-toe all day, and he asks whether several short stops add up. אביי asks רבה about someone who rushes out the long way in the time of the short way, and רבה answers that the long way always makes him חייב. רבי זירא then challenges רבה from the rule that a טמא כהן who serves gets מיתה, showing that such a case only works if the measure is a fixed time. The challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Does the tarrying rule cover lashes too? Left unresolved
steps.stepSummary: This is the second side of a question that began just before this section. Maybe the tradition of שהייה applies to anything inside the מקדש, whether the punishment is a קרבן or מלקות. The question ends with תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps the tradition is that tarrying is required inside the Temple, whether the result is an offering or lashes? Let it stand unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a question that started earlier: is שהייה needed only before someone brings a קרבן, or also before he gets מלקות? It cannot decide, so it says תיקו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first side, said just before this section, was that the tradition of שהייה was only taught for a קרבן. That would mean someone liable for מלקות is punished right away. The second side, here, says the tradition is about the place, inside the מקדש. If so, it applies to both kinds of punishment. Since no proof is found either way, the question is left open.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps. This introduces the second side of a question.
We have it as a tradition, a rule passed down rather than learned from a פסוק.
Tarrying. Staying a set amount of time.
Inside, meaning inside the מקדש.
Lashes, the punishment for doing it on purpose.
Let it stand. The question stays unresolved.

steps.confusionAlert: This line begins in the middle of a question. The first side, that שהייה was taught only for a קרבן, was said just before this section.

phrases.english: Or perhaps,
we have a tradition that tarrying is required inside the Temple —
phrases.notes: גמירי means this is a rule handed down from teacher to student, not something learned from a פסוק.

phrases.english: it makes no difference whether it is for an offering
and it makes no difference whether it is for lashes?
Let it stand unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a question that began before this section.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the שהייה tradition tied to a קרבן only, or to the place inside the מקדש, so that it covers מלקות as well?
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Unresolved whether מלקות also needs שהייה.

steps.title: A טמא person hanging in the air of the courtyard
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks about a טמא person who hangs in the air of the עזרה. He stays the right amount of time, but he cannot bow down there. Does that count as שהייה? The question ends with תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked: if he hung himself in the air of the courtyard, what is the law? Perhaps the tradition of tarrying only covers tarrying where bowing is possible, and not tarrying where bowing is impossible. Or perhaps the tradition is about tarrying inside, whether or not bowing is possible? Let it stand unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא tests whether שהייה only counts if the person is in a position where he could bow down. A person floating in the air could not bow. The גמרא cannot decide, so it says תיקו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The length of שהייה is measured by the time it takes to bow down. So maybe the tradition only covers a person who is able to bow. The other side says the tradition is simply about time spent inside the מקדש, so it does not matter whether he can bow.

keyTerms.meaning: He asks, raises a question.
What is the law?
The airspace of the Temple courtyard.
Suited for bowing. A position where one could bow down.

phrases.english: Rava asked:
If he hung himself in the airspace of the courtyard, what is the law?
When we have the tradition about tarrying —
is it tarrying that is suited for bowing,
phrases.notes: The amount of tarrying is the time it takes to bow down. Here he is hanging, so he couldn't actually bow.

phrases.english: but tarrying that is not suited for bowing we have no tradition about;
or perhaps we have a tradition of tarrying inside —
no difference whether it is suited for bowing
and no difference whether it is not suited for bowing?
Let it stand unresolved.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רָבָא: תָּלָה עַצְמוֹ בַּאֲוִיר עֲזָרָה, מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new question that tests a different limit of the same שהייה tradition.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does שהייה count when the person cannot bow down?

steps.title: Someone who made himself impure on purpose inside
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks about someone who made himself טמא on purpose inside the מקדש. Does he also get the allowance of שהייה, or is the tradition only about someone who became טמא by accident? The question ends with תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי asked: if he made himself impure on purpose, what is the law? Perhaps the tradition of tarrying is for one who became impure against his will, and there is no tradition of tarrying for one who did it on purpose. Or perhaps the tradition is about tarrying inside, whether it happened against his will or on purpose? Let it stand unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי asks whether the שהייה rule protects only someone who became טמא against his will. Someone who chose to become טמא inside the מקדש might not be included. The גמרא cannot decide, so it says תיקו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the tradition is about אונס, then the person who acted on purpose (מזיד) is liable right away, with no waiting time. If the tradition is about the place, inside the מקדש, then even he is liable only once he stays long enough.

keyTerms.meaning: He made himself impure.
On purpose.
Against one's will, beyond one's control.
It makes no difference.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi asked:
If he made himself impure on purpose, what is the law?
Is it for one who became impure against his will that we have the tradition of tarrying,
but for one who did it on purpose we have no tradition of tarrying;
or perhaps we have a tradition of tarrying inside the Temple —
no difference whether against his will
and no difference whether on purpose?
Let it stand unresolved.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַב אָשֵׁי: טִימֵּא עַצְמוֹ בְּמֵזִיד, מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another new question about the scope of שהייה. This time it asks about how the טומאה happened.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the שהייה tradition tied to אונס, or to being inside the מקדש?

steps.title: A נזיר at a grave: does he need to tarry before lashes?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks about a נזיר who finds himself at a grave. Does he need שהייה before he gets מלקות? Maybe the tradition is only for inside the מקדש. Or maybe it is for anyone who became טמא against his will. The question ends with תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי asked: a נזיר at a grave, does he need tarrying to get lashes, or not? Perhaps the tradition of tarrying is for inside the Temple, and there is no tradition of tarrying outside. Or perhaps the tradition of tarrying is for one who became impure against his will, whether inside or outside? Let it stand unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי takes the שהייה question outside the מקדש. He asks about a נזיר who becomes טמא at a grave. The גמרא cannot decide, so it says תיקו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Look at how this flips the last question. In step 3, the two sides were אונס against בפנים. Here, בפנים is the narrow side and אונס is the wide side. If the tradition is about the place, the נזיר outside gets no waiting time. If it is about אונס, he also needs שהייה before he gets מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: A nazirite. Among other things, he may not become impure from a dead body.
A grave.
Outside, meaning outside the מקדש.
It is not necessary.

steps.whatToRemember: All four questions test one tradition, שהייה, against different factors: the kind of punishment, being able to bow, אונס against מזיד, and inside against outside. Every one ends with תיקו.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi asked:
A nazirite at a grave,

phrases.aramaic: בָּעֵי שְׁהִיָּיה לְמַלְקוּת אוֹ אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ?
phrases.english: does he need tarrying to get lashes, or does he not need it?
Is it inside the Temple that we have the tradition of tarrying,
but outside we have no tradition of tarrying;
or perhaps we have the tradition of tarrying for one who became impure against his will —
no difference whether inside
and no difference whether outside?
Let it stand unresolved.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַב אָשֵׁי: נָזִיר בְּקֶבֶר, בָּעֵי שְׁהִיָּיה לְמַלְקוּת אוֹ אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same two factors as step 3, but swaps which side is narrow and which is wide.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a נזיר outside the מקדש need שהייה before he gets מלקות?

steps.title: The short way is exempt, even if he walks very slowly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: leaving by the long way makes one חייב, by the short way פטור. רבא explains that the short way stays פטור even if he walks heel-to-toe all day long.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: if he went out the long way, he is liable; the short way, he is exempt. רבא said: the short way that the חכמים meant is exempt even if he walks with his heel touching his toe, even if it takes the whole day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back a line from the משנה about a טמא person leaving the מקדש. רבא explains what 'the short way' means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think the short way is פטור only if he leaves fast. רבא says no: what counts is the route, not the speed. If he takes the shortest path, he is פטור even with tiny steps that take all day.

keyTerms.meaning: The long way, a longer route out of the מקדש
The short way, the most direct route out
Heel next to the big toe, meaning very tiny steps
Liable (here, to bring a קרבן) / exempt

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the questions that follow. רבא's rule is about the route, not the speed, so we now need to ask what happens with stops and with speed on the long way.

phrases.english: If he went out by the longer way, he is liable,
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה about a טמא person leaving the מקדש.

phrases.english: by the shorter way, he is exempt, etc.
Rava said:
The short way that they spoke of —
even if he walks heel next to big toe,
phrases.notes: Each step only moves him forward by the length of his foot, so he moves very slowly.

phrases.english: and even if it takes the whole entire day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the string of תיקו questions, the גמרא goes back to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Leaving by the short route is פטור no matter how slowly he walks.

steps.title: Do separate short stops add up?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks whether several stops, each shorter than the שיעור of שהייה, combine to make a full שהייה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked: periods of staying, do they combine?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks a new question. If a טמא person stops for a short time, moves on, and stops again, do the stops add up to the full time?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each stop alone is too short to make him חייב. The question is whether the חיוב needs one full stop, or whether short stops can be added together to reach the full time.

keyTerms.meaning: Periods of staying or stopping in the מקדש
That they combine or add up together

phrases.english: Rava asked:
Periods of staying, what is the law, do they combine?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new question from the same אמורא, building on the topic of how long a person stays inside.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether several short stops can add up to the full שיעור of שהייה.

steps.title: רבא's own rule should answer this
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: רבא should answer his question from his own rule about heel-to-toe walking.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him answer it from his own statement!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבא's question. It says his own rule from before already seems to answer it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone walking heel-to-toe all day seems to pause between every tiny step. If he is still פטור, it looks like the small pauses do not add up. So why does רבא ask?

keyTerms.meaning: And let him resolve or answer it
From his own (statement)

phrases.english: But let him resolve it from his own statement!
phrases.notes: This means רבא's heel-to-toe rule from the step before.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the question in step 6 by using step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's question about whether stops combine
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Heel-to-toe walking all day includes many tiny pauses, and רבא still says פטור. So pauses seem not to combine, and the question should already be answered.

steps.title: There he never actually stopped
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: in the heel-to-toe case he kept moving and never stopped, so it says nothing about real stops.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is a case where he did not stop.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא's question. The heel-to-toe walker moves slowly but never stands still.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Slow walking is not the same as stopping. רבא's first rule is about steady, slow movement. His question is about someone who really stood still several times, so it stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: There, meaning in the other case
Where he did not stop or stay

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'walking slowly' with 'stopping.' The slow walker is always moving, so he is not doing שהייה at all.

phrases.english: There, it is where he did not stop.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The heel-to-toe walker pauses between steps, so his case would answer whether pauses combine.
steps.terutzMaskana: He never stops at all, so his case cannot answer the question about real stops, and רבא's question stands.

steps.title: Rushing out the long way in the time of the short way
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רבה: if someone takes the long way but goes so fast that it takes only as long as the short way, is he חייב?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי asked רבה: if he went out the long way in the amount of time of the short way, what is the law? Did the tradition teach a time limit, so that if he goes the long way in the time of the short way he is exempt? Or perhaps the tradition was exact: the long way is liable, the short way is exempt?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי asks רבה the opposite of רבא's case. Here the person takes the long route but moves very fast.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is what the הלכה למשה מסיני really measures. If it measures time, a fast trip on the long way is פטור. If it measures the route, the long way is always חייב, however fast he goes.

keyTerms.meaning: A set measure or amount (here, of time)
We learned it as a tradition (from משה)
Exactly, specifically

phrases.english: Abaye asked Rabba:

phrases.aramaic: בָּא לוֹ בַּאֲרוּכָּה שִׁיעוּר קְצָרָה, מַהוּ?
phrases.english: If he went out the long way in the time of the short way, what is the law?
phrases.notes: He ran fast, so the long route took him no longer than walking the short route.

phrases.english: Did we learn a measure of time as the tradition?

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי בָּא לוֹ בַּאֲרוּכָּה שִׁיעוּר קְצָרָה פָּטוּר,
phrases.english: so when he goes the long way in the time of the short way, he is exempt,
or perhaps we learned it exactly:
the long way is liable, the short way is exempt?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new question that is the mirror image of רבא's slow-walker rule: a fast walker on the long way.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the tradition is about time or about the route itself.

steps.title: The long way always makes him liable
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that the חיוב of the long way is not pushed aside for him. Going the long way is חייב, even if he goes fast.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: the long way was not given to be pushed aside for him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers אביי. Taking the long way makes him חייב, no matter how fast he goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה says the rule is about the route, not the clock. The long-way rule stays in force for him even when he rushes, just as רבא said the short way stays פטור even when he walks slowly.

keyTerms.meaning: It was not given
To be pushed aside or cancelled

steps.whatToRemember: The route decides, not the speed. The short way is פטור even when slow (רבא), and the long way is חייב even when fast (רבה).

phrases.english: He said to him:
The long way was not given to be pushed aside for him.
phrases.notes: In plain words: once he took the long way, running fast does not get him out of the חיוב.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לֹא נִתְּנָה אֲרוּכָּה לְהִדָּחוֹת אֶצְלוֹ
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The long way is always חייב. The tradition is about the route, not the time.

steps.title: How can a טמא כהן who serves ever get only מיתה?
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא challenges: we know a טמא כהן who does עבודה gets מיתה בידי שמים. But if he did not stay long enough he could not do any עבודה, and if he did stay long enough he should get כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא objected: but what about the rule we hold, that a טמא person who served gets death? How can you find such a case? If he did not stay, how did he do the service? If he did stay, he is liable to כרת!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא challenges רבה's answer from step 10, that the route and not a set time decides. He uses a known rule about a טמא כהן who serves in the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known rule that a טמא כהן who serves gets מיתה, which is lighter than כרת. If there is no fixed time measure, as רבה said, then staying long enough to do any עבודה should already bring כרת. So when would plain מיתה ever apply? The next step shows how a time-based measure would solve this.

keyTerms.meaning: He objects to it, raises a strong challenge
A טמא כהן who did service in the מקדש
Death at the hand of Heaven (מיתה בידי שמים)
Being cut off, a heavier heavenly punishment
The service done in the מקדש

steps.confusionAlert: מיתה and כרת are two different punishments here. The problem is that the heavier one, כרת, seems to always come first, so the lighter one, מיתה, never gets a case of its own.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira objected to it:
But that which we hold:
a טמא person who served is punished with death;
phrases.notes: This means a כהן who knowingly did the Temple service while טמא.

phrases.english: how can you find such a case?

phrases.aramaic: אִי דְּלָא שְׁהָה – הֵיכִי עָבֵיד עֲבוֹדָה?
phrases.english: If he did not stay, how could he do the service?
If he did stay, he is already liable to כרת!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא, אֶלָּא דְּקַיְימָא לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי זירא challenges רבה's answer in step 10 (route, not time), using the known punishment of a טמא כהן who serves.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's answer in step 10, that the חיוב depends on the route (the long way is always חייב) and not on a set measure of time
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the measure is not a fixed time (as רבה said), any stay long enough to do an עבודה counts as שהייה and brings כרת. Then the rule that a טמא כהן who serves gets only מיתה would never have a case. Step 12 shows that a time-based measure would solve this.

steps.title: If the time limit is a tradition, the case can work
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא grants that if the שיעור of time is a received tradition, we can find a טמא כהן who does עבודה and gets only מיתה בידי שמים. He rushes, does the עבודה, and leaves the short way within the time limit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, if you say the measure of time is known from a tradition, you can find a case. He rushed himself on the short way and did an עבודה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא is spelling out the first half of his challenge from step 11. He shows that one way of understanding the time limit does give us a real case. This sets up the next move, where the other way of understanding it will cause the problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the שיעור (the time to bow down and leave by the short way) is just a fixed amount we received by tradition, then a כהן can beat the clock. He hurries, does the עבודה, and gets out before the time runs out. So he never stayed long enough for כרת, but he still did עבודה while טמא, and he gets מיתה בידי שמים.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, if you say: opens the 'this side works' half of an argument
The measure, the set amount of time
We have it as a tradition, learned from teachers and not from a פסוק
He forced himself, he rushed
The short way out

steps.confusionAlert: This is not רבי זירא's conclusion. A 'בשלמא' line only grants one side. The real difficulty, about the other way of understanding the time limit, comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: Granted, if you say
that the measure is learned as a tradition
phrases.notes: He means the set time a טמא can stay before he is חייב כרת. We would know it from a tradition, not from a פסוק.

phrases.english: you can find it
phrases.notes: Find what? A case of only מיתה בידי שמים, with no כרת.

phrases.english: where he forced himself to rush, using the short way
and performed an עבודה

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the challenge of step 11 by granting that one understanding of the שיעור produces a valid case.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's ruling in step 10 that the measure is the route and not a fixed time. The rule that a טמא כהן who serves gets מיתה only has a case if the measure is a fixed time.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: First half of a 'בשלמא' argument. If the time limit is a tradition, a quick כהן can do עבודה without reaching the כרת time, so the מיתה rule has a case. This prepares the contrast with the other understanding, where no such case would exist.
